Conditional frontier comparison: Donoho (1994) studies optimal recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment, and Stone (1982) supplies the classical smooth-regression benchmark. The present conditional theorem instead couples bounded multiple-response fixed-design observations to an independent full-covariance donor-location experiment. Because historical coordinates are exact and only the external query center is generated, a root-N donor displacement changes a merely lambda-Holder evaluation by order N^{-lambda/2}, producing the N^{-lambda} risk channel without deconvolution. This differs from Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024), where the independently estimated center is a strongly convex minimizer and the minimum-value perturbation is second order. The new content is the joint fixed-design optimal-recovery comparison and its carefully one-sided panel-kernel transfer, not a two-sided conditional theorem over panel-induced laws.

Marginal phase comparison: Stone's (1982) ordinary random-design rate uses a growing collection of distinct design points. Here n_s response replicates occur at only T exact sites, so occupancy creates a separate spacing floor T^{-2lambda/d} under independent dates and {log(T)/T}^{2lambda/d} under allowed geometric-mixing triangular arrays. The replicated-response smoothing term remains bookkeeping but is algebraically dominated by treated replication and spacing for fixed S. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) study generated covariates entering training rows, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study noisy training coordinates and deconvolution. Here training coordinates remain exact; the external donor mean adds N^{-lambda} and changes the oracle/generated-query boundary.

Honest-length comparison: Low (1997) gives the classical coverage-to-testing benchmark, Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) develop modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals, and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) treat dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals. The interval here concentrates one bounded variable per complete unit history, adds an explicit rough-Holder donor-location radius, and is total on geometry failures; it does not require response-calendar mixing or division by estimated variance. Holding training and treated laws fixed while perturbing only donor location yields the additional N^{-lambda/2} expected-length lower channel absent from those benchmarks.
